channel.title: Signal
channel.description: Tech news matched to Patrick's interests, curated daily.

item.title: llama.cpp b12500 adds fastdiv CUDA conv2d optimization
item.description: llama.cpp b12500 swaps three integer divisions for precomputed fast-division in its CUDA conv2d kernel, roughly halving that kernel's runtime on NVIDIA GPUs.

item.title: Spark-X2.6-4B: 4B open model for local agents with adjustable reasoning
item.description: SparkLLM shipped Spark-X2.6-4B, a 4B open model tuned for coding and tool use with a three-level reasoning budget; the GGUF build is 3.54 GB at Q4_K_M and it claims near-9B quality on agent benchmarks.

item.title: The Siege on Manual VTT Layout: Foundry & Fantasy Grounds Are Now Turnkey
item.description: A Basic Fantasy adventure bundle now ships native Foundry VTT and Fantasy Grounds modules compiled by an automated engine in under a minute, replacing manual VTT data entry.

item.title: MACaQ Quantizes One Layer at a Time, Across Inference Backends
item.description: A close read of Huawei's MACaQ quantizer: per-layer calibration for 2-4-bit GGUF and W4A4, with MACaQ-R refining existing GGUF files to a lower KL divergence than Unsloth's equivalent at the same size.

item.title: WoW Forever Raid Release Date: December 9
item.description: Post-launch rundown confirms the first WoW: Forever raids, Barrow Deeps, Hyjal Summit and Onyxia's Lair, unlock December 9 for level 60 players, with the live build on a stack of hotfixes dated through November 13.

item.title: Gemma 4 QAT Checkpoints vs Regular Q4 GGUFs, Measured
item.description: Measured comparison finds Unsloth's QAT GGUF for Gemma 4 E2B the smallest and closest 4-bit file, beating Google's official Q4_0 build.

item.title: Detectify launches Agentic Tooling to bring verifiable evidence to AI-led security investigations
item.description: Detectify's new Agentic Tooling lets teams' own AI agents investigate suspected vulnerabilities in their own environments via MCP and CLI, with a Security Ledger recording verifiable evidence for each finding.

item.title: Qwen Code 1.0 Preview open-sources Alibaba's Agent Harness as an embeddable runtime
item.description: Alibaba folds the production Agent Harness from its Qoder tool into Qwen Code 1.0 Preview, released under Apache-2.0 as an embeddable runtime for multi-step planning, tool orchestration, and failure recovery.

item.title: Detectify launches Agentic Tooling for AI security agents
item.description: Detectify’s new Agentic Tooling lets teams’ own AI agents probe running apps for exploitable flaws, with a Security Ledger recording verifiable evidence of what each agent actually tested.

item.title: Llama.cpp Reaches Version 1.0 Milestone to Standardize Local Open-Source AI Inference
item.description: llama.cpp hits 1.0 after three and a half years, committing to semantic versioning, adding FP8 KV-cache support and smarter MoE expert offloading, and hardening llama-server security.

item.title: Tencent's LoopForge: self-hosted orchestration for coding agents
item.description: Tencent released LoopForge, a Go-based, self-hosted framework for chaining coding agents like Claude Code and Codex, with human approval gates built into the orchestration.

item.title: DeepSeek Releases a Coding AI That Finds and Fixes Bugs on Its Own
item.description: DeepSeek's open-source super-agent prototype runs multiple coding jobs in parallel through a router-and-worker design, cutting slow-case task time nearly in half.

item.title: DeepSeek Harness 0.2.2 adds Codex and Claude delegation
item.description: The open-source DeepSeek Harness (dsh) 0.2.2 release adds an experimental plugin to delegate subtasks to Codex and Claude, plus Git worktrees and six new interface languages.

item.title: Inkling 2 Small VRAM requirements: 393.5 GB official NVFP4, 171.7 GB smallest GGUF
item.description: Thinking Machines' open-weight Inkling 2 Small needs at least 500 GB of VRAM for the official NVFP4 checkpoint, and even the smallest Unsloth GGUF still demands about 172 GB of combined memory.

item.title: Railflare FX: six free sci-fi combat effects for VTTs
item.description: Free pack of six transparent WebM combat effects (drone swarm, EMP burst, railgun beam and more) shipped as a Foundry VTT Sequencer module, usable in other VTTs as plain video files.

item.title: llama.cpp 1.0.0: the local AI engine's first stable release
item.description: After three and a half years of build numbers, llama.cpp ships 1.0.0 with a semver promise — API breaks only on major bumps — plus FP8 KV-cache support, a host-memory MoE expert cache, and new model support.

item.title: Thinking Machines releases Inkling 2 Small open weights under Apache 2.0
item.description: Thinking Machines Lab publishes the weights for Inkling 2 Small, a 594B-parameter MoE with 17B active per token, a week after its hosted-only debut; the NVFP4 checkpoint needs roughly 500GB of GPU memory, so it is a server-class open-weight release rather than a laptop model.

item.title: Semgrep launches agent-native AppSec platform for coding agents
item.description: Semgrep ships an agent-native security platform: its Mandoline engine traces reachable code paths for coding agents, Guardian fixes issues as agents write, and a new MCP server brings the analysis to Codex, Claude Code, and Cursor.

item.title: Ollama on Android: the Termux setup, apps, and models that fit
item.description: Fresh field guide to running Ollama in Termux on a phone, including the official Termux package tracking upstream 0.40.16, Vulkan GPU backends, and which native Android apps fit which models.

item.title: Edge0 releases 145B open model for a single laptop
item.description: Edge0 released Edge0-145B and Edge0-120B on Nov 12: 145B total parameters with 10.12B active per token, derived from Qwen3.8-Flash-Next, weights on Hugging Face under a community license; the vendor's 29GB laptop-memory headline is GPU-side only and its benchmarks are self-reported, not independently verified.

item.title: Inkling 2 Small weights land on Hugging Face under Apache 2.0
item.description: Thinking Machines Lab's 594B MoE (17B active per token) shipped its full weights on November 12 under Apache 2.0, with NVFP4 and MXFP8 checkpoints and local-inference support via SGLang, vLLM and Unsloth.

item.title: WoW Forever Leveling Meta Shift: Class Changes, Quest Gold Rewards, and What's Next
item.description: A week after launch, Blizzard's Nov 10 hotfixes reshaped WoW: Forever leveling: Hunter and Protection Warrior rise, Enhancement Shaman and Warlock fall, and level 48+ quests now pay extra gold.

item.title: Huawei researchers open-source MACaQ quantizer for llama.cpp and vLLM
item.description: Huawei's open-source MACaQ toolkit quantizes text, image, video and audio models down to 2-4 bits, emitting GGUF for llama.cpp and W4A4 for vLLM; its MACaQ-R mode refines an existing GGUF file in place.

item.title: Berkeley and Nvidia open-source coding-agent tools that program industrial robots
item.description: Berkeley and Nvidia released open tools (Graph-as-Policy, RoboSimStudio, VABAR) that let teams of AI coding agents write, simulate, and validate industrial robot programs without collecting robot training data.

item.title: Why AI video generation is turning into an agent loop
item.description: An Oct 29 survey names the agent harness as the runtime wrapped around a model, and the same week Loova, Runway Dev plugins, and ComfyUI shipped that loop as products — with the caveat that none of it is independently tested yet.

item.title: Dolmenwood Premium Game comes to Foundry VTT
item.description: Necrotic Gnome's Dolmenwood fairy-tale setting is now a complete Foundry VTT premium module bundling the Player's, Campaign, Monster, and Maps books on top of the free Dolmenwood system; the same post announces the Beneath the Radiant Dome dungeon adventure.

item.title: World of Warcraft: Forever Sets a Franchise Launch Record: Repositioning a 20-Year-Old Classic
item.description: Blizzard says Forever is the biggest WoW launch ever by peak concurrency and returning players, with 8.86 million characters made in beta and the first raids opening December 9.

item.title: MACaQ quantizer, MACaQ-R: 15% lower KL than Unsloth
item.description: Huawei's open-source MACaQ quantizer ships 2-, 3- and 4-bit GGUF for llama.cpp under Apache 2.0, and its MACaQ-R mode refines an existing Q4_K_XL GGUF to a lower KL divergence than Unsloth's equivalent at the same file size.

item.title: Arete-27B-GGUF: Nous's value-tuned 27B model as a local LLM
item.description: AtomicChat published GGUF builds of Nous Research's Arete-27B, a value-tuned Qwen3.8-27B fine-tune, in quants from 13.6 GB to 28.6 GB with per-file speed and quality measurements.

item.title: TI adds agentic AI to CCStudio, with MCP-driven device data and a migration skill
item.description: Texas Instruments added agentic AI to its CCStudio IDE: MCP servers feed device data and the debugger straight to coding agents, and a device migration skill claims to cut MCU porting from months to days.

item.title: Local LLM With LFM3: 13 Steps, 1 GB, 75 Min [2026]
item.description: Step-by-step walkthrough for running Liquid AI's new LFM3-1.7B locally at 4-bit in about 1 GB, with tool calling and a local OpenAI-compatible endpoint.

item.title: GSQ and RCO: the non-uniform quantization now sitting in GGUF files
item.description: A new per-tensor quantization recipe pairs GSQ's learned low-bit grids with RCO's budget-aware allocation, squeezing Qwen3.8-Flash-Next into a 75.8 GB GGUF that matches the base model on AIME25.

item.title: MACaQ: Huawei open-sources a 4-bit quantizer for GGUF and vLLM
item.description: Huawei's Computing Systems Lab released MACaQ, an Apache-2.0 toolkit that compresses models to 4-bit weights and activations with a layer-by-layer recipe, beating Unsloth's Q4_K_XL on Qwen3.6-35B-A3B fidelity at the same file size.

item.title: GSQ and RCO: per-tensor quantization recipes now shipping in GGUF files
item.description: A writeup of GSQ and RCO, two methods from IST Austria that assign a different quantization type per tensor, letting a 354 GB model ship as a 75.8 GB GGUF file while matching the base model on AIME25.

item.title: llama-cpp-pascal: 50-70% faster inference on old Pascal GPUs
item.description: A llama.cpp fork with hand-written CUDA kernels for pre-tensor-core Pascal cards (GTX 1070 era): compressed-KV flash attention and ternary matmuls, claiming a 27B model at 96K context on an 8GB card.

item.title: ThinkingCap Qwen3.8-Flash-Next GGUF quants land
item.description: GGUF quants of the ThinkingCap finetune of Qwen3.8-Flash-Next, which keeps the base model's answer quality while reasoning in far fewer tokens; Q4_K_M recommended at 113 GB, with Q6_K and Q8_0 options.

item.title: Berkeley open-sources a harness for agents that build robot programs
item.description: UC Berkeley releases Graph-as-Policy, a harness letting coding agents write, simulate in Isaac and revise robot control programs, alongside an industrial-task benchmark.

item.title: On-device AI and small language models: what changed in October and November 2026
item.description: Small models keep shrinking: Taobao open-sourced the 173MB MNN-Pocket-0.3B, Gemini Nano now runs on 140M devices, and on-device inference tooling keeps improving.

item.title: AI Coding Harness: 28 Agents Compared for 2026
item.description: A fresh comparison of 28 coding-agent harnesses against public benchmarks, prices and release data, including OpenCode v2, Claude Code and Codex.

item.title: Liquid AI releases LFM3, a family of 2B-class open-weights models built for local agents
item.description: Liquid AI's LFM3 family gives local agents a 1.7B text model with a 256K context that fits in about 1GB at 4-bit, with day-one llama.cpp and Ollama support.
